2. If M16 (S + catS -> inactive) or M18 (2catS -> inactive) is the true mechanism, deactivation will be immediate and severe from the very beginning of the reaction, because the reactants causing deactivation are at their maximum concentrations.
3. Conversely, if M17 (P + catS -> inactive) or M12 (P + cat -> inactive) is true, the initial reaction rate will be high and uninhibited. Deactivation will only manifest later in the time course as the product naturally accumulates.
Comparing this zero-product progress curve to the previous high-product curve will definitively isolate the product's role in the deactivation pathway while keeping the other variables amplified.
</hypothesis>
